notes: Workflow-tool fan-out. Recipe targets 3 parallel children (a trivial task + `sleep 20` each); the spec hard-asserts only >=2 DISTINCT children both linked within a tight window of the same triggering turn (the schema has no native 'count N' or 'concurrently alive' primitive -- see metadata.json caveats -- so two new_session-constrained parent_linked phases anchored to the SAME parent_turn_start is the strongest concurrency proof the current phase-matching engine supports; it proves genuine fan-out rather than one-at-a-time sequential spawning). Session-birth follows the muse single-birth FilesUnderRoot pattern (2-1/3-1/3-2 precedent): anchored to start UNPINNED. child_a_linked/child_b_linked reuse 3-1's CONTAMINATION guard verbatim (min_delay_ms skips the earliest same-turn ambient skill-reminder/goal-reminder/verify-reminder child). fanout_working mirrors 3-1's intermediate_working: the parent holds working across all children's lifetime (duration_at_least_ms), with no phantom 'journal'/'unknown'-project session ever appearing (narrated only -- the invariants DSL has no 'no session named X' form). parent_turn_end mirrors 3-2's drained_ready: SubagentCount(parent) returning to 0 is implicit in the parent reaching its own final ready (cleanupParentChildrenOnReady), NOT a separate transcript_removed sweep event -- muse never deletes a completed child's session.jsonl from disk (unlike claude-code's journal.jsonl bug shape), so there is no file-removal event to assert here.
